issues.text: When individuals could not be reached for follow-up surveys, their friends and family were interviewed about their whereabouts and earnings. These proxy observations are subject to greater measurement error than self-reported ones, and the authors do not discuss this possibility or how they address it in the regressions that include these observations.
issues.quote: These observations are at an increased risk of measurement error than those where individuals themselves answered the survey. However, the authors do not discuss the possibility of measurement error here, or how to address it

issues.text: The terms of the contract between the labour broker and job seekers are unclear. In particular, it is not stated whether job seekers must pay the contingent agent fee if they receive a job offer but decline it; if they need not, some treatment-group non-migration may reflect cost-based choices rather than the non-pecuniary reasons the authors invoke.
issues.quote: Specifically, do job seekers have to pay the contingent agent fee if they are offered a job but decide not to take it? If not, this could be a reason why some individuals in the treatment group choose to remain in India

issues.text: The paper does not check whether treatment effects of the UAE job offer vary with the contingent agent fee, even though the fee varies considerably across individuals; the evaluator suggests such a heterogeneity analysis if data permit.
issues.quote: If data is available, it would be interesting to check for heterogeneity in the effects of the UAE job offer by the level of contingent agent fee

issues.text: The follow-up classification of individuals (migrated to UAE, stayed in home district, moved to another district in India) omits migration to other foreign countries, and it is unclear whether this option is assumed away or simply absent from the sample.
issues.quote: Here, a fourth option is that individuals migrate to foreign countries other than the UAE. It is unclear whether this option is assumed away, or whether it is simply a feature of the sample

issues.text: In the analysis of effects on social networks, caste or religious group membership (majority or minority status within the region) is not controlled for, although this data could be obtained from the IDHS; the evaluator suggests adding it because minority status may shape attitudes toward new friend groups.
issues.quote: the authors do not control for the individual belonging to a minority or majority caste or religious group within their region. This data is straight-forward to get from the IDHS
